name: call_self_recursively

name: divide_unsigned_32bit
description: Divides a 32-bit dividend by a 32-bit divisor and returns the quotient and the remainder packed into one 64-bit value. A 16-step shift-and-subtract loop handles divisors wider than 16 bits, and a direct 16-bit division handles narrower divisors.

name: copy_sixteen_longs_and_call
description: If the pointer passed on the stack is not null, copies sixteen longwords from a fixed offset in a block addressed by an address register into the buffer it points to. It then makes an indirect call through a code pointer held in another address register, which the call facts tie to a routine that searches a list for a maximum value.

name: write_max_value_header
description: Scans a linked list of entries for the largest value in one field, starting from 149. name: open_graphics_intuition_libraries
description: Opens the graphics and intuition libraries through library calls, using the library names referenced in the file. It sets one flag byte in a structure returned by a library call, makes two further library calls and returns zero.

name: dispatch_hunk_type_records
description: Initialises a block descriptor from a table of values and clears 31 longwords of a buffer. It then loops over records, branching on AmigaDOS hunk type codes such as 1001 to 1007 and 82 and 87 to store fields and call unnamed routines, and it repeats until a set of completion fields is satisfied.

name: check_bitmap_bit_consistency
description: Writes two text characters that show a number into a display buffer, then scans a range of bitmap longwords. For each position it compares a bit test from two bitmap words, calls unnamed routines when the results differ and counts the mismatches in a field, ending with further unnamed calls.

name: copy_memory_via_library
description: Calls a library function through a global base at a fixed negative offset, then makes an indirect call whose target the decompiler could not recover. The facts identify the library function as the exec copy-memory routine.

name: unpack_backward_rle_stream
description: Clears a counter by counting down a 16-bit loop, then decodes a packed byte stream backwards into a destination buffer, expanding two marker bytes into runs of repeated bytes. It then copies 500 longwords to a fixed destination and finishes with a call to a routine at a fixed address.

name: busy_loop_then_trap
description: Runs a fixed-count busy loop that adds a constant to a global variable, then stores the address of the routine itself into that global and issues trap number zero. It is a short startup stub.

name: swap_library_field_and_call
description: Looks up a library base through a library call, saves a pointer field of the structure it returns and replaces that field with the address of a global. It then stores a constant in a global, calls a second library function on another returned base and returns; the file's text names the dos and graphics libraries.

name: configure_cia_then_start
description: Obtains a pointer from a library call and halts in a loop if the pointer is null. Otherwise it calls a library function, sets bits in a CIA control byte with busy-wait delays, polls a custom chip register until one bit clears, sets a DMA control word and clears 848 longwords of a block before calling further routines.

name: forward_control_to_routine
description: Makes a single call to one unnamed routine and then returns, with no arguments or other work. It only forwards control.

name: copy_masked_flag_field
description: When a byte field of the structure equals 1 and the high bit of another byte is set, writes the structure's word field, masked to its low seven bits, through the output pointer. It always returns zero.

name: update_display_frame_state
description: Swaps a pair of display buffer pointers when a flag is set and derives x and y deltas from a potentiometer-style input register. It adds the deltas to two position values clamped to 0 to 319 and 0 to 199, counts down four timers that each write a word and pointer into hardware registers after a short delay, and copies seven longwords into the bitplane pointer registers.

name: update_slot_timers_with_delta
description: Sets a latch byte to 255, then adds byte deltas taken from a word of a record to two position values, clamped to 0 to 319 and 0 to 199. It counts down four timers and, when one reaches one, copies a word and a pointer from the record into hardware registers after a short delay, then copies eight longwords into the bitplane pointer registers.

name: update_slot_timers_on_fire
description: Sets the latch byte to 255 or clears it according to one bit of a global input word, then derives deltas from bit tests on a record field. It clamps two position values, counts down four timers that write record fields to hardware registers after a short delay, and copies eight longwords into the bitplane pointer registers.

name: update_slot_timers_latched
description: Sets a latch byte to 255, derives deltas from bit tests on a record field and clamps two position values to fixed ranges. It counts down four timers that write record fields to hardware registers after a short delay, then copies eight longwords into the bitplane pointer registers.

name: update_slot_timers_plain
description: Derives deltas from bit tests on a record field without touching the latch byte, clamps two position values to fixed ranges and counts down four timers. Each expired timer writes record fields to hardware registers after a short delay, and the routine ends by copying eight longwords into the bitplane pointer registers.

name: update_slot_timers_from_flags
description: Derives position deltas from bit tests on an input word held in a register, clamps two position values to fixed ranges and counts down four timers. Each expired timer writes record fields to hardware registers after a short delay, and the routine ends by copying eight longwords into the bitplane pointer registers.

name: update_slot_timers_on_bit
description: Adjusts the vertical delta when one bit of an input register is set, clamps two position values and counts down four timers. Each expired timer writes record fields to hardware registers after a short delay, and the routine ends by copying eight longwords into the bitplane pointer registers.

name: clamp_y_then_update_timers
description: Clamps the horizontal position to zero when negative and clamps the vertical position to the range zero to 199, then counts down four timers. Each expired timer writes record fields to hardware registers after a short delay, and the routine ends by copying eight longwords into the bitplane pointer registers.

name: clamp_low_y_update_timers
description: Clamps the vertical position to zero when negative, then counts down four timers. Each expired timer writes record fields to hardware registers after a short delay, and the routine ends by copying eight longwords into the bitplane pointer registers.

name: update_slot_timers_only
description: Counts down four timers without changing any position values. Each expired timer writes record fields to hardware registers after a short delay, and the routine ends by copying eight longwords into the bitplane pointer registers.

name: read_and_clear_word_flag
description: Returns the word stored at a fixed global offset and resets that word to zero when it was non-zero. It acts as a read-once flag accessor.

name: open_handle_read_buffer_field
description: Asks a library routine for a handle using a fixed argument of minus two. If that fails it calls a second library function; otherwise it stores a constant in a stack buffer, passes the handle and buffer to a further library routine and returns a longword from offset 124 of the buffer.

name: read_library_buffer_field
description: Points a stack buffer at a fixed location, stores a constant in it, passes it with a handle to a library routine and then the handle to a second library routine. It returns a longword from offset 124 of the buffer.

name: call_with_handle_or_fallback
description: Requests a handle from a library routine using the code 1005 and the first argument. If none is returned it calls a library function with no arguments; otherwise it passes the handle with the second and third arguments to another library function and then to a third one that takes only the handle.

name: call_fallback_library_stub
description: Calls one library function at a fixed offset with no arguments and returns. It has no other logic.

name: call_with_handle_alternate_call
description: Requests a handle using code 1005 from the first argument. When none is returned it calls a library function with no arguments; otherwise it passes the handle with the third and second arguments to a different library function and then to a further one that takes only the handle.

name: call_fallback_library_stub
description: Calls one library function at a fixed offset with no arguments and returns. It has no other logic.

name: call_handle_by_code_pair
description: Requests a handle using code 1005, and when that returns nothing requests one using code 1006 instead. The handle is then passed with the arguments to a library function and released by a further library call.

name: call_handle_for_code_1006
description: Requests a handle using code 1006 from the first argument, passes it with two stored arguments to a library function and then to a second library routine that takes only the handle.

name: emit_mirrored_position_pairs
description: Calls one library routine to start, then steps a counter down to zero. On each step it issues pairs of library calls at positions mirrored about a centre value, while advancing a bound and an increment.

name: emit_stepped_mirror_pairs
description: Issues pairs of library calls at positions mirrored about a value taken from a frame. After each pair it adds a stepped increment to a running bound and moves the counter down by one, stopping when the counter goes negative.

name: emit_mirror_pairs_loop
description: Issues pairs of library calls at mirrored positions for each counter value, then moves the counter down, looping while it is non-negative. It advances a bound and an increment between steps.

name: program_blitter_for_planes
description: Computes a byte address and a width from two pairs of coordinates, then for each of four bitplanes waits until the blitter is free and writes its size, modulo and address registers. It loops while a bit mask shifts to a non-zero value.

name: write_plane_state_per_bit
description: Shifts a bit mask and, for each bit, stores zero or minus one in a block depending on the bit, along with a row address, a column value and a stride. It advances the address by 8000 per plane and waits for a status bit to clear between planes.

name: write_plane_rows_per_bit
description: Loops over a bit mask, storing to a block a word that is zero or minus one depending on the bit, together with a row address, a column value and a stride. It advances the address by 8000 per plane, waits for a status bit to clear between planes and returns when the mask runs out.

name: advance_seeded_counter
description: On first use, seeds a longword from a 16-bit global counter in its upper and lower halves. It then calls a library function, stores its result plus one as the new state and returns that state shifted right by eight bits.

name: forward_control_to_routine
description: Makes a single call to one unnamed routine and then returns, with no arguments or other work. It only forwards control.

name: access_dma_control_register
description: The decompiler timed out, so this description rests only on the listed facts: the routine accesses the DMA control register and is reached through a pointer in data and from unnamed routines. What it reads or writes cannot be established from the evidence.

name: wait_until_flag_clear
description: Spins while a word in a global slot is non-zero and returns once it clears. It is a wait-until-clear loop with no other work.

name: dispatch_pending_words_then_flag
description: Calls one unnamed routine if a first pending word is non-zero and another if a second pending word is non-zero, then sets a global word to minus one.

name: call_two_routines_in_order
description: Calls two unnamed routines one after the other and returns. It has no other logic.

name: blit_five_plane_rows
description: Computes a byte offset and two plane addresses from coordinate pairs, then runs five times: it waits until the blitter is free, writes two address registers and a control word, advances both addresses by 8000 and writes width and modulo values. It sets a global word to a constant before the loop.

name: blit_plane_pairs_by_count
description: Repeats a count held in a register: it waits until the blitter is free, copies two longwords and a word from a record into blitter registers, then advances two stored addresses by 8000 and decrements the count.

name: blit_plane_pairs_until_zero
description: Copies two longwords and a word from a record into blitter registers, advances two stored addresses by 8000 and repeats after waiting for the blitter, stopping when the count reaches zero.

name: call_routine_with_fixed_arguments
description: Calls one unnamed routine with a base address computed from a global slot plus 3720, a value from another slot, zero and the constant 45. It has no other logic.

name: call_routine_with_row_arguments
description: Calls one unnamed routine with an address derived from a global slot plus a row offset of two word slots multiplied by 40, a second slot value, zero and the difference of two word slots.

name: call_routine_with_region_args
description: Calls one unnamed routine with a value from a global slot, an address derived from another global slot plus a row offset of two word slots multiplied by 40, zero, and the difference of two word slots.

name: request_block_or_fallback
description: Asks a library routine for a block using the argument and the fixed code 65539. If the request returns nothing it calls a fallback library function with no arguments, and it returns the result either way.

name: read_longword_from_slot
description: Returns the longword stored at a fixed offset of minus four from a base held in an address register. It has no other logic.

name: stub_return_immediately
description: The pseudo-code is a bare return with no operations, so the routine does nothing. The call facts list one unnamed routine, but no call appears in the code.

name: forward_two_args_to_library
description: Passes its two arguments unchanged to a library function reached through a global base at a fixed negative offset. It has no other logic.

name: setup_interrupt_and_dma_state
description: Calls two unnamed routines, a library function, and then two further unnamed routines with one library call between them. It writes constants to a global word and calls a library function with a count of five and a pointer, and the facts show it touches the DMA control and interrupt enable registers.

name: store_library_result_slot
description: Calls a library function with the constant 2 and stores its return value in a global slot.

name: setup_input_device_request
description: Requests two values from a library routine using fixed codes and calls a fallback when either is zero. It then stores pointers and constants into a global structure, sets up a request and makes further library calls, including one that touches the interrupt enable register; the file text names dos.library, graphics.library and input.device.

name: pass_stored_blocks_with_sizes
description: Walks a six-entry table, multiplying each entry by ten, and passes every non-null stored pointer with its size to one library function. It then passes about twenty further non-null slots, each with a fixed or stored size, to the same function and finishes with four library calls on stored handles.

name: pass_stored_handles_to_library
description: Passes a stored value to a library function, calls an unnamed routine, then passes two stored handles to a second library function.

name: copy_bytes_overlap_safe
description: Copies a count of bytes between two buffers, walking backward when the source precedes the destination so overlapping regions copy correctly, and forward otherwise. It returns when the count reaches zero.

name: copy_bytes_forward
description: Copies bytes one at a time from a source to a destination for a count held in a data register, advancing both pointers forward until the count reaches minus one. It has no other logic.

name: copy_words_overlap_safe
description: Copies a count of 16-bit words between two buffers, walking backward when the source precedes the destination so overlapping regions copy correctly, and forward otherwise. It returns when the count reaches zero.

name: copy_words_forward
description: Copies 16-bit words one at a time from a source to a destination for a count held in a data register, advancing both pointers forward until the count reaches minus one. It has no other logic.

name: compute_absolute_value
description: Returns the absolute value of a signed 16-bit argument by negating it when it is below zero and returning it unchanged otherwise.

name: compute_absolute_longword
description: Returns the absolute value of a signed longword argument, negating it when it is below zero and returning it unchanged otherwise.

name: multiply_then_divide_packed
description: Multiplies the two 16-bit halves of the first argument and divides the product by the low 16-bit half of the second. It returns the remainder in the upper 16 bits and the quotient in the lower 16 bits of the result.

name: sum_of_word_squares
description: Returns the sum of the squares of the two 16-bit halves of its argument, computed as signed values.

name: multiply_two_words
description: Returns the product of the two 16-bit halves of its argument, computed as signed values. It has no other logic.

name: sample_three_slot_pairs
description: Calls one unnamed routine twice for each of three global slots and stores each returned word in a neighbouring global word, six results in total. It then returns without a value of its own.

name: shift_word_history_after_calls
description: Calls an unnamed routine three times, then saves a word from one global slot, calls another routine and stores its returned word in a second global slot while moving the saved word into the first.

name: sample_into_pair_buffer
description: Calls an unnamed routine twice with the same global slot, then calls a third routine, and stores the returned word and the first argument into the two words of the buffer passed in.

name: stub_return_immediately
description: Does nothing and returns at once. The routine is an empty stub with no calls or operations in its code.

name: lookup_quarter_wave_table
description: Adds 360 to an angle argument, reduces it modulo 1440 and folds the result into a quarter-wave using symmetry. It looks up a 16-bit value in a table reached through a global base and negates it when a sign flag derived from the input is clear.

name: lookup_folded_table_value
description: Reduces an angle argument modulo 1440 and folds it into a quarter-wave using symmetry. It looks up a 16-bit value in a table reached through a global base and negates it when a sign flag derived from the input register is clear.

name: scale_four_offsets_by_divisor
description: Adds 600 to a divisor argument, then stores four values, each a sum or difference of global offsets and arguments shifted left by nine and divided by that divisor. It performs fixed-point scaling of four offsets.

name: scale_two_offsets_by_divisor
description: Stores two values, each a global offset plus an argument shifted into a high word and divided by a divisor formed from another argument plus 600. The results go into two global words.

name: add_packed_bcd_digits
description: Adds a four-byte argument into a four-byte packed BCD number, one byte at a time from the lowest, adjusting each byte back to decimal after the addition. It returns no value of its own.

name: add_bcd_counter_track_max
description: Stores its argument in a global longword, adds four bytes of that value into a packed BCD counter with decimal adjustment, and raises a stored maximum to the counter when the counter is larger. It then calls an unnamed routine.

name: increment_bcd_byte_then_call
description: Stores one in a global byte, adds it into a packed BCD byte with decimal adjustment, then calls an unnamed routine. It has no other logic.
